name: Pont de la Concorde
short_description: Late-18th-century Seine arch bridge built partly with masonry from the demolished Bastille, linking Place de la Concorde to the Assemblée Nationale.

_pipeline.address: Pont de la Concorde, 75007 / 75008 Paris (between Quai des Tuileries and Quai d'Orsay)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Symbolic Revolution-era bridge incorporating Bastille stones; key sightline between Concorde and the National Assembly.

name: Cimetière de Passy
short_description: Small aristocratic Right-Bank cemetery opened in 1820 with an Art Deco entrance and burials including Debussy, Manet, Givenchy, and Berthe Morisot.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Compact cemetery with very high famous-burial density per square metre, near Trocadéro — strong fit for Hidden History and Music Heritage lenses.

name: Pont d'Iéna
short_description: Napoleonic five-arch stone bridge of 1808–1814 linking the Eiffel Tower to the Trocadéro Gardens, pedestrianised since the 2024 Olympics.

_pipeline.address: Pont d'Iéna, 75007 / 75016 Paris (between Quai Branly and Port de la Bourdonnais)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Iconic Eiffel Tower–Trocadéro axis bridge; commemorates Napoleon's 1806 victory at Jena and once threatened with demolition by Blücher.

name: Opéra Bastille
short_description: Carlos Ott-designed modern opera house inaugurated on 13 July 1989 with 2,745 seats, the principal stage of the Opéra national de Paris.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Bicentenary commission by Mitterrand on the site of the former Bastille railway station; principal venue of the Paris Opera.

name: Rue du Pas-de-la-Mule
short_description: Short Marais street built in 1604 alongside Place des Vosges, named after a mounting block once used by nobles arriving on muleback at the Château des Tournelles.
name_variations: rue du Pas de la Mule

_pipeline.address: Rue du Pas-de-la-Mule, 75003 / 75004 Paris (from 31 boulevard Beaumarchais to 22 Place des Vosges)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Hinge street between boulevard Beaumarchais and Place des Vosges; preserved 17th-century fabric of the original Marais grid.

name: Quai de la Mégisserie
short_description: Right-bank Seine quay laid out in 1369, long known for the leather tanners and bird-and-pet shops that still cluster between Châtelet and the Pont Neuf.

_pipeline.address: Quai de la Mégisserie, 75001 Paris (between Pont au Change and Pont Neuf)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Atmospheric riverside walk lined with garden and pet shops; one of the oldest commercial quays in Paris.

name: Rue Sauval
short_description: Short street near Les Halles whose No. 2 is traditionally identified as the birthplace of Molière in 1622.

_pipeline.address: Rue Sauval, 75001 Paris (between rue Saint-Honoré and rue Coquillière)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Reputed birthplace of Molière (No. 2) and a remnant of the medieval street pattern around the old Halles.

name: Place du Marché Sainte-Catherine
short_description: Quiet rectangular Marais square laid out in 1784 on the site of a demolished 13th-century priory and used as an open-air market until 1939.

_pipeline.address: Place du Marché Sainte-Catherine, 75004 Paris (off rue Saint-Antoine)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Pedestrian café square hidden a few steps off rue Saint-Antoine; classic Marais 'secret place' frequently in walking-tour itineraries.

name: Théâtre de la Ville
short_description: Davioud-designed 1862 theatre on Place du Châtelet that Sarah Bernhardt directed for 24 years and which reopened after renovation in 2023 as the Théâtre de la Ville - Sarah Bernhardt.
name_variations: Théâtre de la Ville - Sarah Bernhardt

discovery_sources: Théâtre de la Ville official site
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Twin Châtelet theatre indelibly tied to Sarah Bernhardt's late career, with a rich Belle Époque and contemporary-dance programming history.

name: Passage Saint-Paul
short_description: Quiet Marais passageway running from rue Saint-Paul to a side entrance of the Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis church, on land once part of the Hôtel de la Rochepot.

_pipeline.address: Passage Saint-Paul, 75004 Paris (from 43 rue Saint-Paul to the side door of Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Concealed pedestrian shortcut through the Village Saint-Paul antiques district; a hidden Marais tour beat.

name: Port de l'Arsenal
short_description: Former cargo basin converted in 1983 into a 177-berth pleasure-boat marina linking the Bastille end of the Canal Saint-Martin to the Seine.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Tree-lined leisure marina at the foot of the Bastille — gateway between the Seine and Canal Saint-Martin and a popular waterside walk.

name: Colonne de Juillet
short_description: 47-metre bronze column at the centre of Place de la Bastille (1835–1840) commemorating the Trois Glorieuses of July 1830, with a crypt holding the remains of 615 revolution victims.
name_variations: Génie de la Liberté (figure on top)

discovery_sources: Un jour de plus à Paris
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Centerpiece of the Place de la Bastille; commemorates the 1830 revolution and serves as a rallying point for political demonstrations.

name: Statue de Beaumarchais
short_description: 1895 bronze statue by Louis Clausade depicting the playwright Pierre-Augustin Caron de Beaumarchais arms-crossed, inaugurated in 1897 near his former Marais residence.
name_variations: Statue de Pierre-Augustin Caron de Beaumarchais

_pipeline.address: Square at the corner of rue Saint-Antoine and rue des Tournelles, 75004 Paris (near 4 boulevard Beaumarchais)
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Discreet bronze tribute to the author of The Marriage of Figaro, sited near his former Marais home; a quiet stop linking literary and revolutionary lenses.
